subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use and narrow catch

question: Should plugin-runtime session mutations fail closed on all ownerless rows, and should this PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103534 land through one shared authoritative-row ownership contract?
rationale: The choice determines both the security trust boundary and whether existing plugins can continue using legacy or user-created sessions; automation cannot safely choose that upgrade policy.

options.title: Canonical fail-closed guard
options.body: Approve exact owner equality including ownerless-row rejection, fix the selected-agent reauthorization defect, and coordinate create, patch, reset, and delete around one helper.

options.title: Migration before enforcement
options.body: Define a doctor or explicit ownership migration for legitimate legacy rows before enabling fail-closed enforcement across all mutation methods.

options.title: Pause the ownership rollout
options.body: Hold both PRs until the plugin session trust model and legacy-row authority are explicitly documented.

recommendation.title: Canonical fail-closed guard
recommendation.body: Approve exact owner equality including ownerless-row rejection, fix the selected-agent reauthorization defect, and coordinate create, patch, reset, and delete around one helper.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent session-handler refactor established the current owner boundaries and this choice spans multiple newly split session mutation modules.
